transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having some trouble with eating after really long days. It’s not every second or anything, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but after a day on site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll come home and eat way more than I meant to. Like leftover takeout, cereal, chips—just whatever’s around—and then I end up uncomfortably full. I wasn’t sure if that was something I should bring up, but it’s been bothering me.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever try to compensate for it—like making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Um… I don’t use laxatives or anything like that. And I wouldn’t say I’m, like, exercising excessively. But… yeah, sometimes after those nights I panic a little, and I’ve gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up.

It’s not all the time—maybe a few times a month. I know that probably sounds bad. I just get this feeling like I’ve undone all the work I put into looking put-together, and I want to fix it quickly.
How often do you find yourself making yourself throw up after eating more than you intended?

I mean… if I’m being honest, when I look back over the last few months, it’s probably averaged about once a week. Not like every single week exactly—some weeks it doesn’t happen at all, and then another week it might happen twice. But overall… yeah, about weekly, I guess.

When you make yourself throw up after eating more than you intended, is it mainly because you feel you’ve eaten too much, or is it more because you’re worried about gaining weight or how your body looks?

I’d like to say it’s just because I feel too full, and that is part of it, but… if I’m being honest, it’s more tied up with worrying how I look.

Since I started wearing more fitted work clothes and being up front at meetings, I catch myself kind of judging the whole day by whether my pants feel tight or whether I think people can see my stomach. That sounds a little vain, I know, but that’s where my mind goes. So after I eat too much, it feels like I need to undo it before it shows, I guess.
How often do you find yourself eating a lot more than you intended, without making yourself sick afterwards?

Um… probably more often than I’d like to admit. Not always with making myself sick afterward.

What made me bring it up is that after really long days on site, or after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll get home and kind of… just keep eating. Like leftover takeout, cereal, chips—whatever’s there. And then suddenly I’m uncomfortably full and thinking, why did I do that?

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… it does happen.
Over the past few months, how often would you say you’ve had episodes where you eat a lot more than you intended, even without making yourself sick afterward?

I guess… maybe around once a week? I don’t want to make it sound like it’s constant, because it’s not every day or anything. But what made me bring it up is that after some long days on site, or after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll come home and eat way more than I meant to—leftover takeout, cereal, chips, whatever’s there—until I’m uncomfortably full.

So… yeah, if that counts, I’d say about weekly, give or take.
Do you usually eat this way when you’re alone, or do you find yourself hiding it because you feel ashamed or guilty about how much you’re eating?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… it’s not like I’m sneaking around in some dramatic way, if that makes sense.

It does tend to happen more when I’m by myself, but I don’t know if that’s because I’m hiding it or just because that’s when I’m home and kind of off-duty. I do feel embarrassed afterward, though. Like I wouldn’t really want someone watching me eat that much. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During these episodes when you eat more than you intended, do you ever feel like you can't stop yourself or that you're out of control while you're eating?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t love saying that, because it sounds worse than I want it to.

But on those evenings, once I start, it can feel kind of like I’m on autopilot. I’ll be telling myself, “Okay, stop, you have an early crew start tomorrow,” and then somehow I’m back in the kitchen getting more anyway.

It’s not like every single time, but… yes, there are times where it feels hard to stop.
Do these episodes of eating more than you intend usually leave you feeling really upset, anxious, or distressed afterward?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d say really distressed every time. I don’t want to overstate it.

Usually afterward I feel kind of gross and disappointed in myself, like, “Why did I do that again?” And then I try to just clean up and go to bed or distract myself. Sometimes I’m anxious about it, but I’m not sure if it counts as the kind of distress you mean.
Do you find yourself feeling particularly upset, embarrassed, or ashamed specifically about the way you eat during these episodes, even if you’re by yourself?

I’m not sure I can separate it that neatly. I mean, I do feel embarrassed afterward, but it’s more like… embarrassed that I let it get away from me, not necessarily some specific thing about how I looked eating or anything.

I guess if someone were there, I’d be mortified, so maybe that says something. But when I’m alone, it’s more this quiet shame or disappointment, and then I try not to think about it too much. Does that answer it?
When you find yourself eating more than you intended, does it usually happen all in one sitting—like within a couple of hours—or does it spread out more throughout the evening?

Usually it’s more like one stretch, I think. Like, I get home after a long day on site or after a neighborhood meeting, and then it kind of happens over the evening but not all night—more like I’ll start with leftover takeout, then cereal, chips, whatever’s there, and before I know it I’ve eaten way more than I meant to.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s enough that I end up uncomfortably full. Does that make sense?
When you're eating more than you intended, do you feel like you can't control yourself or stop eating, even if you want to?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying that, because it makes it sound like I’m completely out of control, and it’s not every single time.

But on those evenings, once I start, it can feel kind of like I’m on autopilot. I’ll be telling myself, “Okay, stop, you have an early crew start tomorrow,” and then somehow I’m back in the kitchen getting more anyway. I do want to stop, I just… don’t always seem to make myself stop right then.
Can you recall a specific time when you felt like you couldn’t stop eating, even though you wanted to? What was going through your mind during that time?

Yeah… I can think of one, though it feels kind of embarrassing to say.

It was after a workday where I had an early crew start the next morning, and I remember thinking, like, “Okay, you need to stop now, you have to be up early.” But I’d already started eating, and it just felt like I was on autopilot. I’d tell myself I was done, and then a few minutes later I’d be back in the kitchen getting more.

It wasn’t like I was making some big decision each time. It was more like I knew I wanted to stop, but in the moment I just… didn’t. If that makes sense.
